newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices extend gains.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices extend gains.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Friday extended gains on a shortage of ready stock and dwindling arrivals, dealers said.
"Mill buying improved as millers are now trying to buy more cotton at the current level before prices go up further," a broker said.
Daily arrivals of cotton in the Punjab region dropped to 400/500 bales (170 kg each). In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned rose by 15 rupees at 1,790/1,900 rupees per maund (37.32 kg).
Bengal-deshi rose by 15/20 rupees at 990/1,025 rupees per maund and F-414 rose by the same margin at 2,030/2,050 rupees per maund.

Gujarat cotton also bounced back after a downward correction on Thursday. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose by 200 rupees at 14,500/15,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton rose by 100 rupees at 13,300 rupees and Kala-ginned rose by 300 rupees at 13,000 rupees per candy.
